635	def verify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
636	    failures: list[str] = []
637	    exit_report: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
638	    report: dict[str, Any] = {
639	        "schema": REPORT_SCHEMA,
640	        "passed": False,
641	        "failures": failures,
642	    }
643	    bundle = args.bundle.resolve(strict=True)
644	    plan_path = bundle / "plan.json"
645	    package_path = bundle / "package-inventory.json"
646	    prepare_path = bundle / "prepare-metadata.json"
647	    settings_path = bundle / "settings.json"
648	    weights_path = bundle / "historical-weights.json"
649	    inventory_paths = sorted((bundle / "inventories").glob("*.inventory.json"))
650	    if not inventory_paths:
651	        raise ValueError("bundle contains no compiled inventories")
652	    inventories = plan_shards.load_inventories(inventory_paths)
653	    plan = read_json(plan_path)
654	    if not isinstance(plan, dict):
655	        raise ValueError("plan is not an object")
656	    settings = plan_shards.load_settings(settings_path)
657	    if plan.get("shardCount") != settings.get("shardCount"):
658	        failures.append("bundled settings shard count differs from plan")
659	    for key in (
660	        "timeout",
661	        "commandLineLimit",
662	        "shuffle",
663	        "testParallel",
664	        "goMaxProcs",
665	        "defaultWeightSeconds",
666	    ):
667	        if plan.get("settings", {}).get(key) != settings.get(key):
668	            failures.append(f"bundled setting {key} differs from plan")
669	    if plan.get("historicalWeights", {}).get("sha256") != plan_shards.sha256_file(weights_path):
670	        failures.append("bundled historical-weight hash differs from plan")
671	
672	    prepare = read_json(prepare_path)
673	    if not isinstance(prepare, dict) or prepare.get("schema") != PREPARE_SCHEMA:
674	        failures.append("unexpected prepare metadata schema")
675	    else:
676	        verify_prepare_operation_exits(
677	            prepare,
678	            {inventory["importPath"] for inventory in inventories},
679	            str(prepare_path),
680	            failures,
681	            exit_report,
682	        )
683	        if prepare.get("repositorySha") != plan.get("repositorySha"):
684	            failures.append("prepare repository SHA differs from plan")
685	        if prepare.get("repositoryShaAfter") != plan.get("repositorySha"):
686	            failures.append("prepare post-run repository SHA differs from plan")
687	        if prepare.get("goVersion") != plan.get("goVersion"):
688	            failures.append("prepare Go version differs from plan")
689	        if prepare.get("targetEnvironment") != TARGET_ENVIRONMENT:
690	            failures.append("prepare target is not exactly windows/amd64 with CGO_ENABLED=1")
691	        if prepare.get("targetEnvironment") != plan.get("targetEnvironment"):
692	            failures.append("prepare target differs from plan")
693	        if prepare.get("trackedWorktreeCleanBefore") is not True:
694	            failures.append("prepare did not prove a clean tracked worktree before execution")
695	        if prepare.get("trackedWorktreeCleanAfter") is not True:
696	            failures.append("prepare did not prove a clean tracked worktree after execution")
697	        if not isinstance(prepare.get("goToolDirectory"), str) or not prepare["goToolDirectory"]:
698	            failures.append("prepare omitted its resolved Go tool directory")
699	
700	    for inventory in inventories:
701	        binary = bundle / "binaries" / inventory["binaryName"]
702	        if not binary.is_file():
703	            failures.append(f"compiled binary is missing: {inventory['binaryName']}")
704	            continue
705	        if binary.stat().st_size != inventory["binarySizeBytes"]:
706	            failures.append(f"compiled binary size differs from inventory: {inventory['binaryName']}")
707	        if plan_shards.sha256_file(binary) != inventory["binarySha256"]:
708	            failures.append(f"compiled binary hash differs from inventory: {inventory['binaryName']}")
709	
710	    assignment_for_root, process_assignments, root_details = validate_plan(
711	        plan, inventories, failures
712	    )
713	    package_inventory = read_json(package_path)
714	    if not isinstance(package_inventory, dict) or package_inventory.get("schema") != PACKAGE_SCHEMA:
715	        raise ValueError("unexpected target-Windows package inventory schema")
716	    if package_inventory.get("repositorySha") != plan.get("repositorySha"):
717	        failures.append("package inventory repository SHA differs from plan")
718	    if package_inventory.get("goVersion") != plan.get("goVersion"):
719	        failures.append("package inventory Go version differs from plan")
720	    package_target = {
721	        "GOOS": package_inventory.get("goos"),
722	        "GOARCH": package_inventory.get("goarch"),
723	        "CGO_ENABLED": package_inventory.get("cgoEnabled"),
724	    }
725	    if package_target != TARGET_ENVIRONMENT:
726	        failures.append("package inventory target is not exactly windows/amd64 with CGO_ENABLED=1")
727	    if package_target != plan.get("targetEnvironment"):
728	        failures.append("package inventory target differs from plan")
729	    package_rows = package_inventory.get("packages")
730	    if not isinstance(package_rows, list) or not package_rows:
731	        raise ValueError("target-Windows package inventory is empty")
732	    package_names: set[str] = set()
733	    heavy_names: set[str] = set()
734	    for row in package_rows:
735	        if not isinstance(row, dict) or not isinstance(row.get("heavy"), bool):
736	            raise ValueError("target-Windows package inventory contains a malformed row")
737	        package = row.get("importPath")
738	        if not isinstance(package, str) or not package or package in package_names:
739	            raise ValueError("target-Windows package inventory contains a missing or duplicate package")
740	        package_names.add(package)
741	        if row["heavy"]:
742	            heavy_names.add(package)
743	    if heavy_names != set(root_details):
744	        failures.append("target-Windows heavy package declarations differ from compiled inventories")
745	    configured_test_mains = {
746	        item["importPath"]: item["expectedTestMainDeclarations"]
747	        for item in settings["heavyPackages"]
748	    }
749	    inventory_test_mains = {
750	        item["importPath"]: item["testMainDeclarations"] for item in inventories
751	    }
752	    if configured_test_mains != inventory_test_mains:
753	        failures.append("compiled TestMain declarations differ from bundled settings")
754	
755	    report["shards"] = verify_shards(
756	        args.shard_results.resolve(strict=True),
757	        plan,
758	        plan_shards.sha256_file(plan_path),
759	        inventories,
760	        assignment_for_root,
761	        process_assignments,
762	        root_details,
763	        failures,
764	        exit_report,
765	    )
766	    report["otherPackages"] = verify_other(
767	        args.other_results.resolve(strict=True),
768	        plan,
769	        plan_shards.sha256_file(plan_path),
770	        package_inventory,
771	        plan_shards.sha256_file(package_path),
772	        failures,
773	        exit_report,
774	    )
775	    report["inventory"] = {
776	        "repositorySha": plan.get("repositorySha"),
777	        "goVersion": plan.get("goVersion"),
778	        "targetEnvironment": plan.get("targetEnvironment"),
779	        "packageCount": len(package_names),
780	        "heavyPackageCount": len(heavy_names),
781	        "runnableRootCount": len(assignment_for_root),
782	        "excludedBenchmarkCount": sum(len(item["excludedBenchmarks"]) for item in inventories),
783	        "historicallyWeightedCount": plan.get("historicalWeights", {}).get("usedCount"),
784	        "defaultWeightedCount": plan.get("historicalWeights", {}).get("defaultedCount"),
785	    }
786	    report["exitCodes"] = exit_report
787	    report["passed"] = not failures
788	    return report

791	def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
792	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
793	    parser.add_argument("--bundle", type=Path, required=True)
794	    parser.add_argument("--shard-results", type=Path, required=True)
795	    parser.add_argument("--other-results", type=Path, required=True)
796	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
797	    return parser.parse_args(argv)
798	
799	
800	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
801	    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
802	    try:
803	        report = verify(args)
804	    except (ValueError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
805	        report = {"schema": REPORT_SCHEMA, "passed": False, "failures": [str(error)]}
806	    try:
807	        write_json(args.output, report)
808	    except OSError as error:
809	        print(f"error: cannot write report {args.output}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
810	        return 2
811	    if not report.get("passed"):
812	        for failure in report.get("failures", []):
813	            print(f"FAIL: {failure}", file=sys.stderr)
814	        return 1
815	    print("Windows shard coverage and integrity verification passed")
816	    return 0
817	
818	
819	if __name__ == "__main__":
820	    raise SystemExit(main())

import json
import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


REPOSITORY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
WORKFLOW = REPOSITORY / ".github" / "workflows" / "test.yml"
SETTINGS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "settings.json"


class WorkflowContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_windows_monolith_is_replaced_but_native_build_remains(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        test_block = workflow.split("  test:\n", 1)[1].split("  windows-test-prepare:\n", 1)[0]
        build_block = workflow.split("  build:\n", 1)[1].split("  test:\n", 1)[0]
        self.assertIn("os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]", test_block)
        self.assertNotIn("windows-latest", test_block)
        self.assertIn("os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]", build_block)

    def test_dynamic_matrix_and_stable_aggregate_check_are_present(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        settings = json.loads(SETTINGS.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(settings["shardCount"], 8)
        self.assertIn("fromJSON(needs.windows-test-prepare.outputs.shard-matrix)", workflow)
        self.assertIn("name: test (windows-latest)", workflow)
        self.assertIn("windows-test-verify.result", workflow)

    def test_windows_components_follow_the_existing_test_name_scheme(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        component_names = [
            "compile and plan",
            "shard ${{ matrix.shard }}",
            "non-heavy packages",
            "vet",
            "coverage and integrity",
        ]
        for component_name in component_names:
            self.assertIn(
                f"name: test (windows-latest) / {component_name}", workflow
            )
        self.assertNotIn("name: Windows test /", workflow)

    def test_workflow_uses_only_ephemeral_hosted_runners_and_no_baseline(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8").lower()
        self.assertNotIn("self-hosted", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("monolithic-baseline", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("baseline-events", workflow)
        self.assertIn("permissions:\n  contents: read", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("-test.bench", workflow)

    def test_shards_restore_cache_budget_and_verifier_runs_after_prepare(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        shard_block = workflow.split("  windows-test-shards:\n", 1)[1].split(
            "  windows-test-other:\n", 1
        )[0]
        verify_block = workflow.split("  windows-test-verify:\n", 1)[1].split(
            "  windows-test:\n", 1
        )[0]
        self.assertIn("timeout-minutes: 105", shard_block)
        self.assertIn("cache-dependency-path: go.sum", shard_block)
        self.assertNotIn("cache: false", shard_block)
        self.assertIn("needs.windows-test-prepare.result == 'success'", verify_block)
        self.assertNotIn("needs.windows-test-shards.result == 'success'", verify_block)

    def test_every_workflow_python_command_disables_bytecode_writes(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        commands = [
            line.strip()
            for line in workflow.splitlines()
            if re.search(r"(?:^|[& ])python(?: |$)", line)
        ]
        self.assertTrue(commands)
        for command in commands:
            self.assertRegex(command, r"(?:^|[& ])python -B(?: |$)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
HELPER = SCRIPT_DIR / "inventory_testmain.go"


class TestMainInventoryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_helper(self, directory: Path, source: bytes):
        file_name = "lifecycle_windows_test.go"
        (directory / file_name).write_bytes(source)
        payload = {
            "Dir": str(directory.resolve()),
            "TestGoFiles": [file_name],
            "XTestGoFiles": [],
        }
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["go", "run", str(HELPER)],
            input=json.dumps(payload),
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            check=False,
        )
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        return json.loads(completed.stdout)

    def test_lf_and_crlf_declarations_have_the_same_normalized_hash(self):
        declaration = (
            "func TestMain(m *testing.M) {\n"
            "\tif os.Getenv(\"MARKER\") != \"\" {\n"
            "\t\tos.Exit(23)\n"
            "\t}\n"
            "\tos.Exit(m.Run())\n"
            "}"
        )
        source = (
            "package fixture\n\n"
            "import (\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\n"
            + declaration
            + "\n"
        )
        expected = hashlib.sha256(declaration.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as first, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as second:
            lf = self.run_helper(Path(first), source.encode("utf-8"))
            crlf = self.run_helper(Path(second), source.replace("\n", "\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(lf, crlf)
        self.assertEqual(
            lf["declarations"],
            [
                {
                    "file": "lifecycle_windows_test.go",
                    "normalizedSourceSha256": expected,
                }
            ],
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPT_DIR))

import plan_shards  # noqa: E402
import prepare  # noqa: E402
import run_shard  # noqa: E402


def normalized_inventory(package, binary, roots):
    return {
        "importPath": package,
        "packageArgument": "./heavy",
        "packageDirectoryRelative": "internal/heavy",
        "binaryName": binary,
        "binarySha256": "a" * 64,
        "binarySizeBytes": 123,
        "repositorySha": "b" * 40,
        "goVersion": "go version go1.26.7 windows/amd64",
        "targetEnvironment": dict(plan_shards.TARGET_ENVIRONMENT),
        "listingContract": {
            "arguments": ["-test.paniconexit0", "-test.list=."],
            "paniconexit0": True,
            "pwdMatchesPackageDirectory": True,
            "goToolDirectoryPrependedToPath": True,
        },
        "testMainDeclarations": [],
        "roots": roots,
        "excludedBenchmarks": ["BenchmarkNotRun"],
    }


def settings(package="example/heavy", binary="heavy.test.exe", shard_count=2):
    return {
        "schema": plan_shards.SETTINGS_SCHEMA,
        "shardCount": shard_count,
        "defaultWeightSeconds": 1.0,
        "timeout": "30m",
        "commandLineLimit": 30000,
        "shuffle": "off",
        "testParallel": None,
        "goMaxProcs": None,
        "heavyPackages": [
            {
                "argument": "./heavy",
                "importPath": package,
                "binaryName": binary,
                "expectedTestMainDeclarations": [],
            }
        ],
    }


class PlanShardTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_listing_includes_default_roots_and_excludes_benchmarks(self):
        roots, benchmarks = prepare.classify_listing(
            ["TestAlpha", "ExampleThing", "FuzzBytes", "BenchmarkParser"], "fixture"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            roots,
            [
                {"name": "ExampleThing", "kind": "Example"},
                {"name": "FuzzBytes", "kind": "Fuzz"},
                {"name": "TestAlpha", "kind": "Test"},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(benchmarks, ["BenchmarkParser"])

    def test_listing_rejects_testmain_noise_and_duplicates(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "unexpected"):
            prepare.classify_listing(["TestMain", "TestAlpha"], "fixture")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "duplicate"):
            prepare.classify_listing(["TestAlpha", "TestAlpha"], "fixture")

    def test_plan_is_deterministic_complete_and_defaults_new_roots(self):
        inventory = normalized_inventory(
            "example/heavy",
            "heavy.test.exe",
            [
                {"name": "TestSlow", "kind": "Test"},
                {"name": "ExampleCurrent", "kind": "Example"},
                {"name": "FuzzCurrent", "kind": "Fuzz"},
                {"name": "TestNew", "kind": "Test"},
            ],
        )
        weights = {("example/heavy", "TestSlow"): 10.0}
        metadata = {"path": "weights.json", "sha256": "c" * 64, "entryCount": 1}
        first = plan_shards.create_plan([inventory], settings(), weights, metadata)
        second = plan_shards.create_plan([inventory], settings(), weights, metadata)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        assigned = {
            (assignment["importPath"], root["name"]): root
            for shard in first["shards"]
            for assignment in shard["assignments"]
            for root in assignment["roots"]
        }
        self.assertEqual(len(assigned), 4)
        self.assertEqual(assigned[("example/heavy", "TestSlow")]["weightSource"], "historical-windows")
        self.assertEqual(assigned[("example/heavy", "TestNew")]["weightSource"], "default-current-inventory")
        self.assertEqual(first["historicalWeights"]["defaultedCount"], 3)

    def test_compressed_regex_selects_exact_roots(self):
        names = ["TestParser", "TestParserDepth", "ExampleParser", "FuzzParser"]
        expression = plan_shards.compressed_run_regex(names)
        compiled = re.compile(expression)
        self.assertEqual({name for name in names if compiled.fullmatch(name)}, set(names))
        for name in ("BenchmarkParser", "Test", "TestParserExtra", "Fuzz"):
            self.assertIsNone(compiled.fullmatch(name))

    def test_settings_fail_closed_on_semantic_overrides(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            path = Path(directory) / "settings.json"
            value = settings()
            value["shuffle"] = "on"
            path.write_text(json.dumps(value), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "shuffle"):
                plan_shards.load_settings(path)

    def test_utf16_command_budget_counts_non_bmp_units_and_nul(self):
        units = run_shard.command_line_utf16_units("C:\\go.exe", ["arg", "😀"])
        serialized = 'C:\\go.exe arg 😀'
        self.assertEqual(units, len(serialized.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2 + 1)

    def test_direct_binary_arguments_include_paniconexit0_and_cmd_go_environment(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory).resolve()
            package = root / "package"
            tool = root / "tool"
            package.mkdir()
            tool.mkdir()
            binary = root / "heavy.test.exe"
            listing = prepare.direct_listing_arguments(binary)
            shard = run_shard.shard_command_arguments(
                "example/heavy", binary, "30m", "^TestA$", None
            )
            self.assertIn("-test.paniconexit0", listing)
            self.assertIn("-test.paniconexit0", shard)
            self.assertNotIn("-test.testlogfile", listing)
            self.assertNotIn("-test.testlogfile", shard)
            for build_environment in (
                prepare.direct_test_environment,
                run_shard.direct_test_environment,
            ):
                environment = build_environment({"PATH": "original"}, package, tool)
                self.assertEqual(environment["PWD"], str(package))
                self.assertEqual(environment["PATH"].split(os.pathsep)[0], str(tool))

import json
import re
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


REPOSITORY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
WORKFLOW = REPOSITORY / ".github" / "workflows" / "test.yml"
SETTINGS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "settings.json"


class WorkflowContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_windows_monolith_is_replaced_but_native_build_remains(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        test_block = workflow.split("  test:\n", 1)[1].split("  windows-test-prepare:\n", 1)[0]
        build_block = workflow.split("  build:\n", 1)[1].split("  test:\n", 1)[0]
        self.assertIn("os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]", test_block)
        self.assertNotIn("windows-latest", test_block)
        self.assertIn("os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]", build_block)

    def test_dynamic_matrix_and_stable_aggregate_check_are_present(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        settings = json.loads(SETTINGS.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(settings["shardCount"], 8)
        self.assertIn("fromJSON(needs.windows-test-prepare.outputs.shard-matrix)", workflow)
        self.assertIn("name: test (windows-latest)", workflow)
        self.assertIn("windows-test-verify.result", workflow)

    def test_windows_components_follow_the_existing_test_name_scheme(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        component_names = [
            "compile and plan",
            "shard ${{ matrix.shard }}",
            "non-heavy packages",
            "vet",
            "coverage and integrity",
        ]
        for component_name in component_names:
            self.assertIn(
                f"name: test (windows-latest) / {component_name}", workflow
            )
        self.assertNotIn("name: Windows test /", workflow)

    def test_workflow_uses_only_ephemeral_hosted_runners_and_no_baseline(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8").lower()
        self.assertNotIn("self-hosted", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("monolithic-baseline", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("baseline-events", workflow)
        self.assertIn("permissions:\n  contents: read", workflow)
        self.assertNotIn("-test.bench", workflow)

    def test_shards_restore_cache_budget_and_verifier_runs_after_prepare(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        shard_block = workflow.split("  windows-test-shards:\n", 1)[1].split(
            "  windows-test-other:\n", 1
        )[0]
        verify_block = workflow.split("  windows-test-verify:\n", 1)[1].split(
            "  windows-test:\n", 1
        )[0]
        self.assertIn("timeout-minutes: 105", shard_block)
        self.assertIn("cache-dependency-path: go.sum", shard_block)
        self.assertNotIn("cache: false", shard_block)
        self.assertIn("needs.windows-test-prepare.result == 'success'", verify_block)
        self.assertNotIn("needs.windows-test-shards.result == 'success'", verify_block)

    def test_every_workflow_python_command_disables_bytecode_writes(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        commands = [
            line.strip()
            for line in workflow.splitlines()
            if re.search(r"(?:^|[& ])python(?: |$)", line)
        ]
        self.assertTrue(commands)
        for command in commands:
            self.assertRegex(command, r"(?:^|[& ])python -B(?: |$)")

import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
HELPER = SCRIPT_DIR / "inventory_testmain.go"


class TestMainInventoryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_helper(self, directory: Path, source: bytes):
        file_name = "lifecycle_windows_test.go"
        (directory / file_name).write_bytes(source)
        payload = {
            "Dir": str(directory.resolve()),
            "TestGoFiles": [file_name],
            "XTestGoFiles": [],
        }
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["go", "run", str(HELPER)],
            input=json.dumps(payload),
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            check=False,
        )
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        return json.loads(completed.stdout)

    def test_lf_and_crlf_declarations_have_the_same_normalized_hash(self):
        declaration = (
            "func TestMain(m *testing.M) {\n"
            "\tif os.Getenv(\"MARKER\") != \"\" {\n"
            "\t\tos.Exit(23)\n"
            "\t}\n"
            "\tos.Exit(m.Run())\n"
            "}"
        )
        source = (
            "package fixture\n\n"
            "import (\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\n"
            + declaration
            + "\n"
        )
        expected = hashlib.sha256(declaration.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as first, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as second:
            lf = self.run_helper(Path(first), source.encode("utf-8"))
            crlf = self.run_helper(Path(second), source.replace("\n", "\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(lf, crlf)
        self.assertEqual(
            lf["declarations"],
            [
                {
                    "file": "lifecycle_windows_test.go",
                    "normalizedSourceSha256": expected,
                }
            ],
        )

import json
import os

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPT_DIR))

import plan_shards  # noqa: E402
import prepare  # noqa: E402
import run_shard  # noqa: E402


def normalized_inventory(package, binary, roots):
    return {
        "importPath": package,
        "packageArgument": "./heavy",
        "packageDirectoryRelative": "internal/heavy",
        "binaryName": binary,
        "binarySha256": "a" * 64,
        "binarySizeBytes": 123,
        "repositorySha": "b" * 40,
        "goVersion": "go version go1.26.7 windows/amd64",
        "targetEnvironment": dict(plan_shards.TARGET_ENVIRONMENT),
        "listingContract": {
            "arguments": ["-test.paniconexit0", "-test.list=."],
            "paniconexit0": True,
            "pwdMatchesPackageDirectory": True,
            "goToolDirectoryPrependedToPath": True,
        },
        "testMainDeclarations": [],
        "roots": roots,
        "excludedBenchmarks": ["BenchmarkNotRun"],
    }


def settings(package="example/heavy", binary="heavy.test.exe", shard_count=2):
    return {
        "schema": plan_shards.SETTINGS_SCHEMA,
        "shardCount": shard_count,
        "defaultWeightSeconds": 1.0,
        "timeout": "30m",
        "commandLineLimit": 30000,
        "shuffle": "off",
        "testParallel": None,
        "goMaxProcs": None,
        "heavyPackages": [
            {
                "argument": "./heavy",
                "importPath": package,
                "binaryName": binary,
                "expectedTestMainDeclarations": [],
            }
        ],
    }


class PlanShardTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_listing_includes_default_roots_and_excludes_benchmarks(self):
        roots, benchmarks = prepare.classify_listing(
            ["TestAlpha", "ExampleThing", "FuzzBytes", "BenchmarkParser"], "fixture"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            roots,
            [
                {"name": "ExampleThing", "kind": "Example"},
                {"name": "FuzzBytes", "kind": "Fuzz"},
                {"name": "TestAlpha", "kind": "Test"},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(benchmarks, ["BenchmarkParser"])

    def test_listing_rejects_testmain_noise_and_duplicates(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "unexpected"):
            prepare.classify_listing(["TestMain", "TestAlpha"], "fixture")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "duplicate"):
            prepare.classify_listing(["TestAlpha", "TestAlpha"], "fixture")

    def test_plan_is_deterministic_complete_and_defaults_new_roots(self):
        inventory = normalized_inventory(
            "example/heavy",
            "heavy.test.exe",
            [
                {"name": "TestSlow", "kind": "Test"},
                {"name": "ExampleCurrent", "kind": "Example"},
                {"name": "FuzzCurrent", "kind": "Fuzz"},
                {"name": "TestNew", "kind": "Test"},
            ],
        )
        weights = {("example/heavy", "TestSlow"): 10.0}
        metadata = {"path": "weights.json", "sha256": "c" * 64, "entryCount": 1}
        first = plan_shards.create_plan([inventory], settings(), weights, metadata)
        second = plan_shards.create_plan([inventory], settings(), weights, metadata)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        assigned = {
            (assignment["importPath"], root["name"]): root
            for shard in first["shards"]
            for assignment in shard["assignments"]
            for root in assignment["roots"]
        }
        self.assertEqual(len(assigned), 4)
        self.assertEqual(assigned[("example/heavy", "TestSlow")]["weightSource"], "historical-windows")
        self.assertEqual(assigned[("example/heavy", "TestNew")]["weightSource"], "default-current-inventory")
        self.assertEqual(first["historicalWeights"]["defaultedCount"], 3)

    def test_compressed_regex_selects_exact_roots(self):
        names = ["TestParser", "TestParserDepth", "ExampleParser", "FuzzParser"]
        expression = plan_shards.compressed_run_regex(names)
        compiled = re.compile(expression)
        self.assertEqual({name for name in names if compiled.fullmatch(name)}, set(names))
        for name in ("BenchmarkParser", "Test", "TestParserExtra", "Fuzz"):
            self.assertIsNone(compiled.fullmatch(name))

    def test_settings_fail_closed_on_semantic_overrides(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            path = Path(directory) / "settings.json"
            value = settings()
            value["shuffle"] = "on"
            path.write_text(json.dumps(value), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "shuffle"):
                plan_shards.load_settings(path)

    def test_utf16_command_budget_counts_non_bmp_units_and_nul(self):
        units = run_shard.command_line_utf16_units("C:\\go.exe", ["arg", "😀"])
        serialized = 'C:\\go.exe arg 😀'
        self.assertEqual(units, len(serialized.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2 + 1)

    def test_direct_binary_arguments_include_paniconexit0_and_cmd_go_environment(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = Path(directory).resolve()
            package = root / "package"
            tool = root / "tool"
            package.mkdir()
            tool.mkdir()
            binary = root / "heavy.test.exe"
            listing = prepare.direct_listing_arguments(binary)
            shard = run_shard.shard_command_arguments(
                "example/heavy", binary, "30m", "^TestA$", None
            )
            self.assertIn("-test.paniconexit0", listing)
            self.assertIn("-test.paniconexit0", shard)
            self.assertNotIn("-test.testlogfile", listing)
            self.assertNotIn("-test.testlogfile", shard)
            for build_environment in (
                prepare.direct_test_environment,
                run_shard.direct_test_environment,
            ):
                environment = build_environment({"PATH": "original"}, package, tool)
                self.assertEqual(environment["PWD"], str(package))
                self.assertEqual(environment["PATH"].split(os.pathsep)[0], str(tool))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Target identities served by the production test-sharding harness.

Everything that differs between the supported native targets lives here, so
the prepare, plan, run, and verify code paths stay shared. A target is always
named explicitly (the `--target` argument, pinned by the workflow) and must
agree with the settings file and every artifact; nothing infers it from the
host, and an unknown or mismatched target fails closed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import struct
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Mapping, Sequence


# Windows: CreateProcess rejects a serialized command line longer than 32767
# UTF-16 code units, including the terminating NUL.
WINDOWS_COMMAND_LINE_MAXIMUM = 32767

# macOS: execve(2) fails with E2BIG when the argument area exceeds ARG_MAX
# (NCARGS in <sys/syslimits.h>, `getconf ARG_MAX`), which is 1048576 bytes on
# every supported Darwin release. That area holds the NUL-terminated argv AND
# environment strings plus one pointer per string, so a settings limit is a
# budget for argv alone and may never claim the whole area. Darwin has no
# separate per-string limit (Linux does: MAX_ARG_STRLEN, 131072 bytes).
DARWIN_ARG_MAX = 1048576


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Target:
    name: str
    goos: str
    goarch: str
    host_platform: str
    host_label: str
    binary_suffix: str
    weight_source: str
    posix: bool
    command_line_metric: str
    command_line_unit: str
    command_line_limit_maximum: int

    @property
    def environment(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"CGO_ENABLED": "1", "GOARCH": self.goarch, "GOOS": self.goos}

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.name} with CGO_ENABLED=1"

    def valid_command_line_limit(self, value: Any) -> bool:
        return (
            isinstance(value, int)
            and not isinstance(value, bool)
            and 1024 <= value <= self.command_line_limit_maximum
        )

    def command_line_cost(self, executable: str, arguments: Sequence[str]) -> int:
        """Size of one launch in the unit the target's kernel limit is stated in."""
        if self.posix:
            return sum(len(os.fsencode(item)) + 1 for item in (executable, *arguments))
        serialized = subprocess.list2cmdline([executable, *arguments])
        return len(serialized.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2 + 1


WINDOWS_AMD64 = Target(
    name="windows/amd64",
    goos="windows",
    goarch="amd64",
    host_platform="win32",
    host_label="Windows",
    binary_suffix=".test.exe",
    weight_source="historical-windows",
    posix=False,
    command_line_metric="commandLineUtf16Units",
    command_line_unit="UTF-16 units",
    command_line_limit_maximum=WINDOWS_COMMAND_LINE_MAXIMUM,
)

DARWIN_ARM64 = Target(
    name="darwin/arm64",
    goos="darwin",
    goarch="arm64",
    host_platform="darwin",
    host_label="macOS",
    binary_suffix=".test",
    weight_source="historical-darwin",
    posix=True,
    command_line_metric="commandLineArgvBytes",
    command_line_unit="argv bytes",
    # Half of ARG_MAX is the most a settings file may hand to argv; the rest
    # is reserved for the environment and the pointer arrays.
    command_line_limit_maximum=DARWIN_ARG_MAX // 2,
)

DEFAULT = WINDOWS_AMD64
TARGETS = {target.name: target for target in (WINDOWS_AMD64, DARWIN_ARM64)}


def resolve(name: Any) -> Target:
    if not isinstance(name, str) or name not in TARGETS:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported target {name!r}; supported: {sorted(TARGETS)!r}")
    return TARGETS[name]


def argument_area_maximum() -> int:
    """The running kernel's exec argument-area size (POSIX hosts only)."""
    return int(os.sysconf("SC_ARG_MAX"))


def argument_area_bytes(arguments: Sequence[str], environment: Mapping[str, str]) -> int:
    """Bytes execve must copy: argv and environment strings plus their pointers."""
    strings = sum(len(os.fsencode(item)) + 1 for item in arguments)
    strings += sum(
        len(os.fsencode(key)) + len(os.fsencode(value)) + 2 for key, value in environment.items()
    )
    pointers = struct.calcsize("P") * (len(arguments) + len(environment) + 2)
    return strings + pointers


def checked_argument_area(
    target: Target, arguments: Sequence[str], environment: Mapping[str, str], label: str
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Fail closed when a POSIX launch cannot fit beside its environment.

    The settings limit bounds argv; this bounds argv plus the runner's actual
    environment against the kernel's own figure, so a large environment can
    never turn an in-budget command into a truncated or refused launch.
    """
    if not target.posix:
        return {}
    used = argument_area_bytes(arguments, environment)
    maximum = argument_area_maximum()
    if used > maximum:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{label} needs {used} bytes of exec argument area, above the kernel limit {maximum}; "
            "refusing implicit batching"
        )
    return {"execArgumentAreaBytes": used, "execArgumentAreaLimit": maximum}


def valid_argument_area(target: Target, record: Any) -> bool:
    """Whether a run record carries the argument-area evidence its target requires."""
    if not target.posix:
        return True
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return False
    used, maximum = record.get("execArgumentAreaBytes"), record.get("execArgumentAreaLimit")
    return (
        isinstance(used, int)
        and not isinstance(used, bool)
        and isinstance(maximum, int)
        and not isinstance(maximum, bool)
        and 1 <= used <= maximum
    )

# macOS: execve(2) fails with E2BIG when the argument area exceeds ARG_MAX
# (NCARGS in <sys/syslimits.h>, `getconf ARG_MAX`), which is 1048576 bytes on
# every supported Darwin release. That area holds the NUL-terminated argv AND
# environment strings plus one pointer per string, so a settings limit is a
# budget for argv alone and may never claim the whole area. Darwin has no
# separate per-string limit (Linux does: MAX_ARG_STRLEN, 131072 bytes).
DARWIN_ARG_MAX = 1048576


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Target:
    name: str
    goos: str
    goarch: str
    host_platform: str
    host_label: str
    binary_suffix: str
    weight_source: str
    posix: bool
    command_line_metric: str
    command_line_unit: str
    command_line_limit_maximum: int

    @property
    def environment(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"CGO_ENABLED": "1", "GOARCH": self.goarch, "GOOS": self.goos}

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.name} with CGO_ENABLED=1"

    def valid_command_line_limit(self, value: Any) -> bool:
        return (
            isinstance(value, int)
            and not isinstance(value, bool)
            and 1024 <= value <= self.command_line_limit_maximum
        )

    def command_line_cost(self, executable: str, arguments: Sequence[str]) -> int:
        """Size of one launch in the unit the target's kernel limit is stated in."""
        if self.posix:
            return sum(len(os.fsencode(item)) + 1 for item in (executable, *arguments))
        serialized = subprocess.list2cmdline([executable, *arguments])
        return len(serialized.encode("utf-16-le")) // 2 + 1


WINDOWS_AMD64 = Target(
    name="windows/amd64",
    goos="windows",
    goarch="amd64",
    host_platform="win32",
    host_label="Windows",
    binary_suffix=".test.exe",
    weight_source="historical-windows",
    posix=False,
    command_line_metric="commandLineUtf16Units",
    command_line_unit="UTF-16 units",
    command_line_limit_maximum=WINDOWS_COMMAND_LINE_MAXIMUM,
)

DARWIN_ARM64 = Target(
    name="darwin/arm64",
    goos="darwin",
    goarch="arm64",
    host_platform="darwin",
    host_label="macOS",
    binary_suffix=".test",
    weight_source="historical-darwin",
    posix=True,
    command_line_metric="commandLineArgvBytes",
    command_line_unit="argv bytes",

def resolve(name: Any) -> Target:
    if not isinstance(name, str) or name not in TARGETS:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported target {name!r}; supported: {sorted(TARGETS)!r}")
    return TARGETS[name]


def argument_area_maximum() -> int:
    """The running kernel's exec argument-area size (POSIX hosts only)."""
    return int(os.sysconf("SC_ARG_MAX"))


def argument_area_bytes(arguments: Sequence[str], environment: Mapping[str, str]) -> int:
    """Bytes execve must copy: argv and environment strings plus their pointers."""
    strings = sum(len(os.fsencode(item)) + 1 for item in arguments)
    strings += sum(
        len(os.fsencode(key)) + len(os.fsencode(value)) + 2 for key, value in environment.items()
    )
    pointers = struct.calcsize("P") * (len(arguments) + len(environment) + 2)
    return strings + pointers


def checked_argument_area(
    target: Target, arguments: Sequence[str], environment: Mapping[str, str], label: str
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Fail closed when a POSIX launch cannot fit beside its environment.

    The settings limit bounds argv; this bounds argv plus the runner's actual
    environment against the kernel's own figure, so a large environment can
    never turn an in-budget command into a truncated or refused launch.
    """
    if not target.posix:
        return {}
    used = argument_area_bytes(arguments, environment)
    maximum = argument_area_maximum()
    if used > maximum:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{label} needs {used} bytes of exec argument area, above the kernel limit {maximum}; "
            "refusing implicit batching"
        )
    return {"execArgumentAreaBytes": used, "execArgumentAreaLimit": maximum}


def valid_argument_area(target: Target, record: Any) -> bool:
    """Whether a run record carries the argument-area evidence its target requires."""
    if not target.posix:
        return True
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        return False
    used, maximum = record.get("execArgumentAreaBytes"), record.get("execArgumentAreaLimit")
    return (
        isinstance(used, int)
        and not isinstance(used, bool)
        and isinstance(maximum, int)
        and not isinstance(maximum, bool)
        and 1 <= used <= maximum
    )

class TargetSettingsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_committed_settings_name_one_target_each(self):
        windows = plan_shards.load_settings(WINDOWS_SETTINGS)
        darwin = plan_shards.load_settings(DARWIN_SETTINGS)
        self.assertIs(plan_shards.settings_target(windows), WINDOWS)
        self.assertIs(plan_shards.settings_target(darwin), DARWIN)
        # The Windows file predates the target key and must keep meaning Windows.
        self.assertNotIn("target", json.loads(WINDOWS_SETTINGS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        self.assertEqual(
            [item["importPath"] for item in darwin["heavyPackages"]],
            [item["importPath"] for item in windows["heavyPackages"]],
        )
        for item in windows["heavyPackages"]:
            self.assertTrue(item["binaryName"].endswith(".test.exe"))
        for item in darwin["heavyPackages"]:
            self.assertTrue(item["binaryName"].endswith(".test"))

            self.assertEqual(item["expectedTestMainDeclarations"], [])

        self.assertEqual(plan_shards.load_settings(DARWIN_SETTINGS)["shardCount"], 4)

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "commandLineLimit"):
            load_payload(settings_payload(limit=DARWIN.command_line_limit_maximum + 1))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "commandLineLimit"):

class PosixCommandBudgetTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_argv_cost_counts_encoded_bytes_and_one_nul_per_argument(self):
        cost = DARWIN.command_line_cost("/go/bin/go", ["arg", "\U0001f600", ""])
        self.assertEqual(cost, len(b"/go/bin/go") + 1 + 3 + 1 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 1)
        self.assertEqual(DARWIN.command_line_metric, "commandLineArgvBytes")

    def test_windows_cost_is_still_serialized_utf16_units(self):
        units = WINDOWS.command_line_cost("C:\\go.exe", ["arg", "\U0001f600"])
        self.assertEqual(units, len("C:\\go.exe arg \U0001f600".encode("utf-16-le")) // 2 + 1)
        self.assertEqual(units, run_shard.command_line_utf16_units("C:\\go.exe", ["arg", "\U0001f600"]))
        self.assertEqual(units, run_other.command_line_utf16_units("C:\\go.exe", ["arg", "\U0001f600"]))
        self.assertEqual(WINDOWS.command_line_metric, "commandLineUtf16Units")

    def test_argument_area_counts_environment_and_pointers(self):
        pointer = targets.struct.calcsize("P")
        used = targets.argument_area_bytes(["go", "test"], {"A": "b", "PATH": "/bin"})
        strings = (2 + 1) + (4 + 1) + (1 + 1 + 1 + 1) + (4 + 1 + 4 + 1)
        self.assertEqual(used, strings + pointer * (2 + 2 + 2))

    def test_argument_area_above_the_kernel_limit_fails_closed(self):
        environment = {"BIG": "x" * 4096}
        with mock.patch.object(targets, "argument_area_maximum", return_value=4096):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "exec argument area"):
                targets.checked_argument_area(DARWIN, ["go"], environment, "fixture")
            # Windows has no such area; its budget is the serialized command line.
            self.assertEqual(targets.checked_argument_area(WINDOWS, ["go"], environment, "fixture"), {})
        with mock.patch.object(targets, "argument_area_maximum", return_value=targets.DARWIN_ARG_MAX):
            record = targets.checked_argument_area(DARWIN, ["go"], environment, "fixture")
        self.assertEqual(record["execArgumentAreaLimit"], targets.DARWIN_ARG_MAX)
        self.assertTrue(targets.valid_argument_area(DARWIN, record))
        self.assertFalse(targets.valid_argument_area(DARWIN, {}))
        self.assertFalse(
            targets.valid_argument_area(
                DARWIN, {"execArgumentAreaBytes": 9, "execArgumentAreaLimit": 8}
            )
        )
        self.assertTrue(targets.valid_argument_area(WINDOWS, {}))

    @unittest.skipUnless(hasattr(os, "sysconf"), "POSIX host required")
    def test_host_kernel_limit_is_readable_on_posix_hosts(self):
        self.assertGreaterEqual(targets.argument_area_maximum(), 4096)

    @unittest.skipUnless(sys.platform == "darwin", "macOS host required")
    def test_documented_darwin_arg_max_matches_this_kernel(self):
        self.assertEqual(targets.argument_area_maximum(), targets.DARWIN_ARG_MAX)

class FakeDarwinGo:
    """Stands in for every subprocess.run call made by run_shard.run."""

    def __init__(self, go, tool_directory, environment):
        self.go = go
        self.tool_directory = tool_directory
        self.environment = environment
        self.test_calls = []

    def __call__(self, argv, **kwargs):
        if argv[:1] == ["git"] and "rev-parse" in argv:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, REPOSITORY_SHA + "\n", "")
        if argv[:1] == ["git"] and "status" in argv:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, "", "")
        if argv == [self.go, "version"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, GO_VERSION + "\n", "")
        if argv[:3] == [self.go, "env", "-json"]:
            value = dict(self.environment)
            value["GOTOOLDIR"] = str(self.tool_directory)
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, json.dumps(value), "")
        if argv == [self.go, "clean", "-testcache"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, b"", b"")
        if argv[:3] == [self.go, "tool", "test2json"]:
            self.test_calls.append((list(argv), dict(kwargs)))
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0)
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected subprocess.run call: {argv!r}")

class FakeDarwinGo:
    """Stands in for every subprocess.run call made by run_shard.run."""

    def __init__(self, go, tool_directory, environment):
        self.go = go
        self.tool_directory = tool_directory
        self.environment = environment
        self.test_calls = []

    def __call__(self, argv, **kwargs):
        if argv[:1] == ["git"] and "rev-parse" in argv:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, REPOSITORY_SHA + "\n", "")
        if argv[:1] == ["git"] and "status" in argv:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, "", "")
        if argv == [self.go, "version"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, GO_VERSION + "\n", "")
        if argv[:3] == [self.go, "env", "-json"]:
            value = dict(self.environment)
            value["GOTOOLDIR"] = str(self.tool_directory)
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, json.dumps(value), "")
        if argv == [self.go, "clean", "-testcache"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, b"", b"")
        if argv[:3] == [self.go, "tool", "test2json"]:
            self.test_calls.append((list(argv), dict(kwargs)))
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0)
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected subprocess.run call: {argv!r}")

class FakeDarwinGo:
    """Stands in for every subprocess.run call made by run_shard.run."""

    def __init__(self, go, tool_directory, environment):
        self.go = go
        self.tool_directory = tool_directory
        self.environment = environment
        self.test_calls = []

    def __call__(self, argv, **kwargs):
        if argv[:1] == ["git"] and "rev-parse" in argv:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, REPOSITORY_SHA + "\n", "")
        if argv[:1] == ["git"] and "status" in argv:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, "", "")
        if argv == [self.go, "version"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, GO_VERSION + "\n", "")
        if argv[:3] == [self.go, "env", "-json"]:
            value = dict(self.environment)
            value["GOTOOLDIR"] = str(self.tool_directory)
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, json.dumps(value), "")
        if argv == [self.go, "clean", "-testcache"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, b"", b"")
        if argv[:3] == [self.go, "tool", "test2json"]:
            self.test_calls.append((list(argv), dict(kwargs)))
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0)
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected subprocess.run call: {argv!r}")

class DarwinVerifyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The verifier's coverage and identity checks, replayed for darwin/arm64."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.fixtures = VerifyResultsTests()
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temporary.cleanup)
        self.arguments, self.output, self.bundle, self.shards_root, self.other_root = (
            self.fixtures.make_fixture(Path(self.temporary.name), DARWIN)
        )

    def verify(self, arguments=None):
        code = self.fixtures.run_verifier(self.arguments if arguments is None else arguments)
        return code, json.loads(self.output.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    def mutate(self, path, change):
        payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        change(payload)
        write_json(path, payload)

    def first_shard_metadata(self):
        return sorted(self.shards_root.rglob("shard-metadata.json"))[0]

    def test_complete_darwin_fixture_passes(self):
        self.assertIn("--target", self.arguments)
        self.assertTrue((self.bundle / "binaries" / "heavy.test").is_file())
        code, report = self.verify()
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, report["failures"])
        self.assertTrue(report["passed"])
        self.assertEqual(report["inventory"]["runnableRootCount"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["inventory"]["targetEnvironment"],
            {"GOOS": "darwin", "GOARCH": "arm64", "CGO_ENABLED": "1"},
        )

    def test_darwin_evidence_does_not_verify_as_windows_or_the_reverse(self):
        without_target = self.arguments[: self.arguments.index("--target")]
        code, report = self.verify(without_target)
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertFalse(report["passed"])
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            arguments, output, _, _, _ = self.fixtures.make_fixture(Path(directory))
            code = self.fixtures.run_verifier([*arguments, "--target", DARWIN.name])
            self.assertEqual(code, 1)
            self.assertFalse(json.loads(output.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["passed"])

    def test_target_identity_is_checked_at_every_darwin_artifact_boundary(self):
        def environment(key, value):
            return lambda payload: payload["targetEnvironment"].__setitem__(key, value)

        mutations = (
            ("plan", self.bundle / "plan.json", environment("GOARCH", "amd64")),
            (
                "compiled inventory",
                next((self.bundle / "inventories").glob("*.inventory.json")),
                lambda payload: payload.__setitem__("goos", "linux"),
            ),
            (
                "package inventory",
                self.bundle / "package-inventory.json",
                lambda payload: payload.__setitem__("goarch", "amd64"),
            ),
            ("prepare", self.bundle / "prepare-metadata.json", environment("CGO_ENABLED", "0")),
            ("shard", self.first_shard_metadata(), environment("GOOS", "linux")),
            ("non-heavy", self.other_root / "other-metadata.json", environment("GOARCH", "amd64")),
            (
                "settings",
                self.bundle / "settings.json",
                lambda payload: payload.__setitem__("target", "linux/arm64"),
            ),
        )
        for label, path, change in mutations:
            original = path.read_bytes()
            with self.subTest(label=label):
                self.mutate(path, change)
                code, report = self.verify()
                self.assertEqual(code, 1)
                self.assertTrue(any("target" in failure for failure in report["failures"]))
            path.write_bytes(original)
        self.assertEqual(self.verify()[0], 0)

    def test_missing_root_and_duplicate_run_fail_closed_on_darwin(self):
        events_path = sorted(self.shards_root.rglob("shard-events.jsonl"))[0]
        lines = events_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        run_line = next(line for line in lines if '"run"' in line)
        events_path.write_text("\n".join([*lines, run_line]) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertTrue(any("planned roots" in failure for failure in report["failures"]))

    def test_posix_budget_evidence_is_required_and_bounded(self):
        def drop_argv(payload):
            del payload["invocations"][0]["commandLineArgvBytes"]

        def windows_metric(payload):
            invocation = payload["invocations"][0]
            invocation["commandLineUtf16Units"] = invocation.pop("commandLineArgvBytes")

        def over_argv(payload):
            payload["invocations"][0]["commandLineArgvBytes"] = 262145

        def drop_area(payload):
            del payload["invocations"][0]["execArgumentAreaBytes"]

        def over_area(payload):
            invocation = payload["invocations"][0]
            invocation["execArgumentAreaBytes"] = invocation["execArgumentAreaLimit"] + 1

        shard = self.first_shard_metadata()
        for label, change, fragment in (
            ("argv omitted", drop_argv, "command line exceeded or omitted"),
            ("argv in the Windows unit", windows_metric, "command line exceeded or omitted"),
            ("argv over budget", over_argv, "command line exceeded or omitted"),
            ("area omitted", drop_area, "exec argument area"),
            ("area over limit", over_area, "exec argument area"),
        ):
            original = shard.read_bytes()
            with self.subTest(label=label):
                self.mutate(shard, change)
                code, report = self.verify()
                self.assertEqual(code, 1)
                self.assertTrue(any(fragment in failure for failure in report["failures"]))
            shard.write_bytes(original)

        other = self.other_root / "other-metadata.json"
        for label, change, fragment in (
            (
                "argv omitted",
                lambda payload: payload.pop("commandLineArgvBytes"),
                "non-heavy command line exceeded or omitted",
            ),
            (
                "area omitted",
                lambda payload: payload.pop("execArgumentAreaLimit"),
                "non-heavy exec argument area",
            ),
        ):
            original = other.read_bytes()
            with self.subTest(runner="non-heavy", label=label):
                self.mutate(other, change)
                code, report = self.verify()
                self.assertEqual(code, 1)
                self.assertTrue(any(fragment in failure for failure in report["failures"]))
            other.write_bytes(original)

    def test_binary_and_lifecycle_mutations_fail_closed_on_darwin(self):
        with (self.bundle / "binaries" / "heavy.test").open("ab") as handle:
            handle.write(b"mutated")

        def lifecycle(payload):
            invocation = payload["invocations"][0]
            invocation["paniconexit0"] = False
            invocation["pwdMatchesPackageDirectory"] = False
            invocation["goToolDirectoryPrependedToPath"] = False

        self.mutate(self.first_shard_metadata(), lifecycle)
        code, report = self.verify()
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        failures = "\n".join(report["failures"])
        for fragment in ("binary", "paniconexit0", "PWD", "PATH"):
            self.assertIn(fragment, failures)

S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-m1-Projects-entire-graph/92bc2a98-aded-4d3d-a987-db22b9a68b40/scratchpad; cat > $S/README.md <<'EOF'
# Production native test sharding (Windows and macOS)

This directory keeps its original name, but the harness in it now serves two
native targets with one code path: `windows/amd64` and `darwin/arm64`. Linux
still runs `go test ./...` as a single job.

For each target the `test` workflow compiles the configured CGO test binaries
once on a standard ephemeral runner, inventories every default-runnable root
(`Test`, `Example`, and `Fuzz`, but never `Benchmark`), and assigns those roots
to deterministic weighted shards. The compiled binaries and immutable plan are
downloaded by independent standard runners of the same target, one per shard.

## Targets

`targets.py` is the single definition of what differs between targets. Every
script takes `--target` (default `windows/amd64`, so the Windows invocations
are unchanged); the workflow pins it, and it must agree with the settings file,
the host platform, `go env`, and every artifact.

| | `windows/amd64` | `darwin/arm64` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Settings | `settings.json` | `settings.darwin-arm64.json` |
| Weights | `historical-weights.json` | `historical-weights.darwin-arm64.json` |
| Shards | 8 | 4 |
| Test binaries | `*.test.exe` | `*.test` |
| Command budget | 30000 UTF-16 units | 262144 argv bytes |
| Budget record | `commandLineUtf16Units` | `commandLineArgvBytes` |
| Workflow jobs, artifacts | `windows-test-*` | `macos-test-*` |
| Aggregate required check | `test (windows-latest)` | `test (macos-latest)` |

A settings file names its target with a `target` key; `settings.json` predates
the key and its absence means `windows/amd64`. Inside a bundle the settings and
weights are always stored as `settings.json` and `historical-weights.json`.
The JSON schema identifiers keep their historical `entire-graph.windows-ci.*`
prefix for both targets; the target is carried by `targetEnvironment`.

macOS uses four shards rather than eight because GitHub-hosted macOS
concurrency is capped per account (as low as five concurrent jobs) and the
workflow runs other macOS jobs. Four shards plus the non-heavy job is five.

## Semantics

A target's settings file is its only tuning surface. The defaults preserve
`go test` semantics: shuffle is off, `-parallel` and `GOMAXPROCS` are unset,
and every shard has a 30-minute package timeout. Historical timings only seed
known roots. The inventory produced from the current compiled binary is
authoritative, so a newly added root is always included with the configured
default weight.

Direct test-binary launches preserve the environment and lifecycle details
that `cmd/go` supplies: `PWD` is the absolute package directory, the active
`GOTOOLDIR` is first on `PATH`, and `-test.paniconexit0` is unconditional.
Every shard clears only the Go test-result cache once before execution while
retaining setup-go's module and build caches. Before and after prepare, shard,
and non-heavy execution, the harness requires a clean tracked worktree and an
unchanged commit.

The target identity is fixed to the native target with `CGO_ENABLED=1` through
every inventory, plan, runner record, and verification boundary.
`inventory_testmain.go` parses only the target-selected `TestGoFiles` and
`XTestGoFiles`; settings pin each top-level `TestMain` declaration by filename
and the SHA-256 of its exact AST source range after LF normalization. That
makes lifecycle-hook drift fail closed while remaining stable across LF and
CRLF checkouts. On Windows the pinned declarations live in `*_windows_test.go`
files; Go selects none of those on darwin and no other test file of the heavy
packages declares `TestMain`, so the macOS pins are empty lists and a
`TestMain` that appears later fails the prepare job until it is pinned.

## Command-line budgets

A shard selects its roots with one `-test.run` expression and the harness
refuses to batch implicitly, so each launch is measured against the limit of
its target and fails closed above it.

On Windows the limit is `CreateProcess`'s 32767 UTF-16 units for the serialized
command line; the setting is 30000.

On macOS the constraint is `execve`'s argument area, `ARG_MAX` (1048576 bytes;
`getconf ARG_MAX`, `NCARGS` in `<sys/syslimits.h>`). That area holds the
NUL-terminated argv strings, the environment strings, and one pointer per
string, and Darwin has no separate per-argument limit. `commandLineLimit` is
therefore an argv budget in bytes: 262144, a quarter of `ARG_MAX`, which leaves
three quarters for the environment and pointers (a settings file may claim at
most half). Each launch additionally records `execArgumentAreaBytes` (argv plus
the runner's actual environment plus pointers) against
`execArgumentAreaLimit` (`sysconf(SC_ARG_MAX)` on that runner) and is refused
if it would not fit; the verifier requires both records.

## Artifact transport on macOS

`actions/upload-artifact` stores files without POSIX modes, so downloaded test
binaries are not executable. `run_shard.py` first matches each binary's SHA-256
to the plan and only then restores the owner execute bit, recording
`executableBitRestored`. The mode is not part of the verified identity; the
bytes are.

## Verification

The verifier has no monolithic reference run. It instead fails closed unless
the plan is a disjoint, complete partition of the compiled inventories; every
planned root has exactly one top-level `run` and one successful terminal
event; each package process starts and terminates with the planned
multiplicity; every non-heavy target-selected package runs exactly once; all
binary hashes, repository/toolchain identities, metadata exits, and command
budgets agree. Exit fields are schema-mandated: prepare's top-level result and
every expected operation, each shard's cache clean and planned invocation, and
the non-heavy clean/test sequence must all be present and zero.

The workflow keeps native `go build ./...` coverage on both targets and adds a
separate native `go vet ./...` job for each, because the harness compiles and
runs with `-vet=off` and the lint job vets only the files Go selects on Linux.
It uses only standard ephemeral hosted runners.

## Historical weights

Weights are per target and only balance shards; they never decide what runs.
The Windows file was seeded from a Windows monolithic baseline. The macOS file
was seeded from one sequential local run of the sharded flow on an Apple M1
(darwin/arm64); roots below two seconds use the configured default, as on
Windows. Hosted runners are slower, which scales every shard alike.

## Running a target locally

On a machine of the target platform, at a clean committed checkout:

```sh
H=tools/ci-bench/windows-production; O=$(mktemp -d); SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
python3 -B $H/prepare.py --target darwin/arm64 --repository "$PWD" --output "$O/bundle" \
  --settings $H/settings.darwin-arm64.json --weights $H/historical-weights.darwin-arm64.json \
  --expected-repository-sha "$SHA"
for i in 0 1 2 3; do
  python3 -B $H/run_shard.py --target darwin/arm64 --repository "$PWD" --bundle "$O/bundle" \
    --output "$O/shards/macos-test-shard-$i" --shard-index $i --expected-repository-sha "$SHA"
done
python3 -B $H/run_other.py --target darwin/arm64 --repository "$PWD" --bundle "$O/bundle" \
  --output "$O/other" --expected-repository-sha "$SHA"
python3 -B $H/verify_results.py --target darwin/arm64 --bundle "$O/bundle" \
  --shard-results "$O/shards" --other-results "$O/other" --output "$O/verification.json"
```
EOF

every expected operation, each shard's cache clean and planned invocation, and
the non-heavy clean/test sequence must all be present and zero.

The workflow keeps native `go build ./...` coverage on both targets and adds a
separate native `go vet ./...` job for each, because the harness compiles and
runs with `-vet=off` and the lint job vets only the files Go selects on Linux.
It uses only standard ephemeral hosted runners.

## Historical weights

Weights are per target and only balance shards; they never decide what runs.
The Windows file was seeded from a Windows monolithic baseline. The macOS file
was seeded from one sequential local run of the sharded flow on an Apple M1
(darwin/arm64); roots below two seconds use the configured default, as on
Windows. Hosted runners are slower, which scales every shard alike.

## Running a target locally

On a machine of the target platform, at a clean committed checkout:

```sh
H=tools/ci-bench/windows-production; O=$(mktemp -d); SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
python3 -B $H/prepare.py --target darwin/arm64 --repository "$PWD" --output "$O/bundle" \
  --settings $H/settings.darwin-arm64.json --weights $H/historical-weights.darwin-arm64.json \
  --expected-repository-sha "$SHA"
for i in 0 1 2 3; do
  python3 -B $H/run_shard.py --target darwin/arm64 --repository "$PWD" --bundle "$O/bundle" \
    --output "$O/shards/macos-test-shard-$i" --shard-index $i --expected-repository-sha "$SHA"
done
python3 -B $H/run_other.py --target darwin/arm64 --repository "$PWD" --bundle "$O/bundle" \
  --output "$O/other" --expected-repository-sha "$SHA"
python3 -B $H/verify_results.py --target darwin/arm64 --bundle "$O/bundle" \
  --shard-results "$O/shards" --other-results "$O/other" --output "$O/verification.json"
```

            self.assertNotIn("needs:", vet)

            validate = f'python -B -m unittest discover -s {HARNESS_PATH}/tests -p "test_*.py" -v'
            self.assertIn(validate, prepare)

    def test_artifacts_are_named_per_target_and_never_cross(self):
        for workflow, name, _ in self.for_each_target():
            foreign = next(other for other in SHARDED_TARGETS if other != name)
            prepare = job_block(workflow, f"{name}-test-prepare")
            self.assertIn(f"          name: {name}-test-bundle\n", prepare)
            self.assertIn("if-no-files-found: error", prepare)
            self.assertIn("compression-level: 0", prepare)
            shards = job_block(workflow, f"{name}-test-shards")
            self.assertIn(f"          name: {name}-test-bundle\n", shards)
            self.assertIn(f"          name: {name}-test-shard-${{{{ matrix.shard }}}}\n", shards)
            other = job_block(workflow, f"{name}-test-other")
            self.assertIn(f"          name: {name}-test-bundle\n", other)
            self.assertIn(f"          name: {name}-test-other\n", other)
            verify = job_block(workflow, f"{name}-test-verify")
            self.assertIn(f"          name: {name}-test-bundle\n", verify)
            self.assertIn(f"          pattern: {name}-test-shard-*\n", verify)

                    self.assertIn("        if: always()\n", block)

        for workflow, name, expected in self.for_each_target():

            for component in ("prepare", "shards", "other", "vet"):

        )

            self.assertNotIn("depot-macos", block)
            self.assertNotIn("pwsh", block)
            self.assertNotIn(".exe", block)
        self.assertIn("capped per account", workflow)

        workflow = workflow_text()
        commands = [

            for component in COMPONENTS:
                block = job_block(workflow, f"{name}-test-{component}")
                self.assertEqual(block.count("python "), block.count("python -B "))
